Rashi on Niddah 16a:10:1.hebrew: דכ"ע - אפי' רב מודה דוסתות דאורייתא. והא דקאמר דבמצאתה טהורה — טהורה כשבדקה בשיעור וסת של וסתה, דודאי אי הוה דם הוה משכחא. ושמואל סבר, אפי' הכי טמאה, דאורח בזמנו בא, הואיל ולא בדקה בשעת וסת ממש:
Rashi on Niddah 16a:10:1.english: That everyone - Even Rav agrees that [the concern for] set periods is by Torah law. And that which he says that if she found [herself examined and found it clean], she is pure — [she is pure] when she examined herself within the time-span of her set period, for certainly, had there been blood, she would have found it. But Shmuel holds that even so she is impure, since [a woman's] cycle comes at its proper time, [and] since she did not examine herself at the exact time of the period.

Rashi on Niddah 16a:10:2.hebrew: וכאן שלא בדקה עצמה כו' - הא דקאמר לעיל רב זירא וסתות דאורייתא, וטמאה אפילו לרב, בשלא בדקה עצמה בשיעור וסת, ואח"כ בדקה ומצאתה טהורה — טמאה. ואיכא דאמרי דמר אמר חדא ומר אמר חדא, ולא פליגי:
Rashi on Niddah 16a:10:2.english: And there, where she did not examine herself, etc. - That which [Rabbi Zeira] said above, that the [laws of] periods are by Torah law, and [the woman] is impure even according to Rav, applies where she did not examine herself within the period of time needed for menstruation, and afterward she examined herself and found herself pure — [then] she is impure. And there are those who say that this Master said one thing and that Master said another thing, and they do not disagree:

Rashi on Niddah 16a:12:1.hebrew: טמאה נדה - אם הגיע וסתה ולא בדקה. קסבר: וסתות דאורייתא:
Rashi on Niddah 16a:12:1.english: She is impure as a menstruating woman - If her set time [of menstruation] arrived and she did not examine herself. [Rabbi Eliezer] holds that [the laws of] fixed menstrual cycles are [binding] by Torah law.

Rashi on Niddah 16a:13:1.hebrew: תבדק - לאחר וסתה. אם מצאתה טמאה — טמאה משעת וסתה; ואם טהורה — טהורה:
Rashi on Niddah 16a:13:1.english: She should be examined - After her expected time [of menstruation]. If she found [blood], she is impure from the time of her expected period; [and if she found] clean, she is pure.

Rashi on Niddah 16a:14:1.hebrew: אף אנן נמי תנינא - דלרבי מאיר וסתות דאורייתא:
Rashi on Niddah 16a:14:1.english: We, too, have learned - That according to Rabbi Meir, [the concern for] periods is by Torah law.

Rashi on Niddah 16a:14:2.english: In hiding - Due to fear of robbers and the police [or: informers].

Rashi on Niddah 16a:15:1.hebrew: הרואה דם מחמת מכה - שיש לה במעיה:
Rashi on Niddah 16a:15:1.english: One who sees blood due to a wound - That she has in her innards.

Rashi on Niddah 16a:15:2.hebrew: אפי' בתוך ימי נדתה - כלומר, בימים שהיא למודה לראות, דהיינו שעת עונתה או שעת וסתה:
Rashi on Niddah 16a:15:2.english: Even within the days of her menstruation - That is, in the days in which she is accustomed to see [blood], namely the time of her [regular] period or the time of her set cycle.

Rashi on Niddah 16a:15:3.english: She is pure - For we attribute [the blood] to the wound that is in that place.

Rashi on Niddah 16a:16:1.hebrew: אם יש לה וסת חוששת לוסתה - כלומר, כשאין לה וסת קבוע, מודינא לך שאף על פי שעברה עונתה תולה במכה. אבל אם יש לה וסת קבוע, וראתה ביום וסתה אפי' מחמת מכה, חיישינן שמא טיפת נדה מעורבת בו:
Rashi on Niddah 16a:16:1.english: If she has a fixed cycle, she must be concerned for her cycle - That is to say: when she has no fixed cycle, I concede to you that even if her set time has passed, she attributes [the blood] to the wound. But if she has a fixed cycle, and she saw blood on the day of her cycle, even [if it came] from the wound, we are concerned lest a drop of menstrual blood be mixed in with it.

Rashi on Niddah 16a:18:1.hebrew: מקומו טמא - וכל דם הבא דרך שם, ואפילו אינו דם נדה, הוי אב הטומאה לטמא אדם טומאת ערב, ואם נגעה בטהרות — טמאים. וקאמר ליה רבי כו' ולהקל על דבריו בא. וה"ק: אם יש לה וסת, כלומר, אם אתה אומר לטמאה מפני וסתה, חוששת לוסתה, כלומר יש לך לטמאה טומאת שבעה, והואיל ואינך חושש לכך, שהרי אתה אומר טהורה משום נדה, שוב אין לה טומאה:
Rashi on Niddah 16a:18:1.english: Its place is impure - Any blood that comes through there, even if it is not menstrual blood, is a primary source of impurity (av hatumah), rendering a person impure with the impurity [lasting until] evening; and if she touched pure items, they become impure. And [the Gemara's statement] "Rabbi said to him, etc." comes to be lenient regarding his words. And this is what it means: If she has a set period (vesset) — that is, if you say to deem her impure because of her set period, [and that] she is concerned for her set period — that is, you should deem her impure with the seven-day impurity; and since you are not concerned about that, as you say she is pure with regard to niddah status, she then has no impurity at all.

Rashi on Niddah 16a:1:1.hebrew: כמין נפל - הלכך ספק וספק הוא, דדלמא מעיקרא לאו נפל הוא:
Rashi on Niddah 16a:1:1.english: Similar to a non-viable newborn - Therefore it is a case of uncertainty upon uncertainty, for perhaps originally it was not a non-viable newborn.

Rashi on Niddah 16a:21:1.hebrew: שני עדים - חדשים, על כל תשמיש: אחד לפניו ואחד לאחריו, ולמחר תעיין בהם:
Rashi on Niddah 16a:21:1.english: Two cloths - New ones, for each act of intercourse: one before it and one after it, and the next morning she should inspect them.

Rashi on Niddah 16a:21:2.hebrew: או תשמש לאור הנר - ותבדוק לאחר תשמיש עד שקנחה בו:
Rashi on Niddah 16a:21:2.english: Or she may engage in intercourse by the light of a lamp - and she must examine [herself] after intercourse, until she has wiped herself with it [the cloth].

Rashi on Niddah 16a:21:3.hebrew: דיה בשני עדים כל הלילה - אחד לפני תשמיש ראשון, ואחד לאחר תשמיש אחרון. ואע"ג דמשמשת ולא ידעה אי חזאי ביני וביני, בין לבית שמאי בין לבית הלל, לא איכפת לן, דלא הוצרכו לבדוק אלא לחומר טהרות:
Rashi on Niddah 16a:21:3.english: It is sufficient with two cloths for the whole night - One before the first act of intercourse and one after the last act of intercourse. And even though she has intercourse and does not know whether she saw [blood] in between, according to both Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel, it does not matter to us, since they were required to examine only for the stringency of [ritually pure] food [that requires] purity.

Rashi on Niddah 16a:4:1.hebrew: ודאי גררוהו - הלכך, ודאי וודאי הוא:
Rashi on Niddah 16a:4:1.english: They certainly dragged it - Therefore, it is [a case of] certainty versus certainty.

Rashi on Niddah 16a:5:1.hebrew: וסתות דאורייתא או דרבנן - הא דקיימא לן דבעי בדיקה בשעת וסתה, דאורייתא היא, דאם לא בדקה טמאה, ואפילו בדקה אחר זמן ומצאתה טהורה, דאורח בזמנו בא, ודם חזאי ונפל לקרקע. או דרבנן הוא דאצרכוה, ואם לא בדקה טהורה:
Rashi on Niddah 16a:5:1.english: Are [the laws of] periods Torah-law or rabbinic? - Is that which we hold, that she requires examination at the time of her period, Torah-law — that if she did not examine she is impure, even if she examined after the time and found herself pure, [for we say] the [menstrual] flow came at its [expected] time, and she saw blood that fell to the ground? Or is it rabbinic, that [the Sages] required it of her, and if she did not examine she is pure?

Rashi on Niddah 16a:6:1.hebrew: ולבסוף ראתה - בבדיקה ראשונה שבדקה עצמה לאחר זמן, ומצאתה טמאה:
Rashi on Niddah 16a:6:1.english: And ultimately she saw - In the first examination in which she examined herself after [the set] time, and found herself impure.

Rashi on Niddah 16a:6:2.hebrew: חוששת לוסתה וחוששת לראייתה - אם זמן וסתה קודם מעת לעת של ראייתה, מטמאינן טהרות דוסתה ואילך, דלמא בזמנו בא. ואם מעת לעת של ראייתה קודם לוסתה, דלא שהתה משעת וסתה עד ראייתה מעת לעת, אזלינן בתר ראייה, וטמאה מעת לעת. וקס"ד דה"ה נמי אם בדקה ומצאתה טהורה דחוששת לוסתה, והא דנקט ראתה משום דבעי למימר וחוששת לראייתה:
Rashi on Niddah 16a:6:2.english: She is concerned for her [fixed] period and concerned for her seeing - If the time of her period is earlier than the twenty-four hours [preceding] her seeing, she renders impure the pure items [she handled] from her period onward, lest it came at its [expected] time. But if the twenty-four hours [preceding] her seeing are earlier than her period, [meaning] that she did not wait from the time of her period until her seeing a full twenty-four hours, we follow the seeing, and she is impure for the twenty-four hours. And the initial assumption was that the same applies even if she examined herself and found herself clean — that she is concerned for her period; and the reason [Rav Huna] mentioned that she saw [blood] is because he wished to say "and she is concerned for her seeing."

Rashi on Niddah 16a:7:1.hebrew: טעמא דראתה - דכיון דבבדיקה ראשונה מצאתה טמאה, אם בדקה נמי בשעת וסתה הוה משכחא:
Rashi on Niddah 16a:7:1.english: The reason is that she saw - For since in the first examination she found herself impure, if she had also examined herself at the time of her set period, she would have found [blood].

Tosafot on Niddah 16a:11:1.hebrew: ורב נחמן בר יצחק אמר בוסתות גופייהו פליגי - נראה דהלכה דוסתות דרבנן, דהא רב נחמן בר יצחק דהוא בתראה אית ליה דלרב וסתות דרבנן. ובפ' יש בכור (בכורות דף מט:) פסיק כרב באיסורי. ועוד, דקיימא לן כר' יהושע דבסמוך לגבי רבי אליעזר, וכחכמים לגבי ר' מאיר. ואע"ג דתנן בפ' בנות כותים (לקמן נדה דף לט.) ברישא: דהיתה במחבא, הגיע שעת וסתה ולא בדקה — טמאה, מ"מ נראה דהלכה הוי וסתות דרבנן כדפרישית. ועוד דאיכא דמוקי לה בפרק בנות כותים (שם) כרבי מאיר, וכן פסק בשאלתות דרב אחאי ור"ח. הילכך אשה שיש לה וסת ולא בדקה בשעת וסתה, ואח"כ בדקה ומצאתה טהורה — טהורה לבעלה. ומיהו נראה לכתחלה צריכה לבדוק בשעת הוסת:
Tosafot on Niddah 16a:11:1.english: "And Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: They disagree about the [law of] periods itself" - It appears that the halakha is that [the law of] periods is rabbinic, for Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak, who is the later authority, holds that according to Rav, [the law of] periods is rabbinic. And in the chapter Yesh Bekhor (Bekhorot 49b), [the Gemara] rules like Rav in matters of prohibitions. Furthermore, we hold like Rabbi Yehoshua, in the passage immediately following, against Rabbi Eliezer, and like the Sages against Rabbi Meir. And although we learned in the chapter Benot Kutim (below, Niddah 39a), in the first clause, that [a woman] who was in hiding, [and] the time of her period arrived and she did not examine herself, is impure — nevertheless it appears that the halakha is that [the law of] periods is rabbinic, as I explained. Furthermore, there are those who establish it, in the chapter Benot Kutim (ibid.), as [following] Rabbi Meir, and so Sheiltot of Rav Aḥai and Rabbeinu Ḥananel ruled. Therefore, a woman who has a set period and did not examine herself at the time of her period, and afterward examined herself and found herself pure, is pure for her husband. But it nevertheless appears that [ideally] she must examine herself at the time of the period.

Tosafot on Niddah 16a:17:1.hebrew: ומר סבר וסתות דרבנן - נראה דדוקא במרגשת שבא דם זה מן המכה, ואפ"ה אם זמן וסת הוא, אי וסתות דאורייתא חיישינן שמא גם מן המקור בא הדם. אבל אם אינה מרגשת יציאת דם מן המכה, טמאה לכ"ע אם הוא זמן וסתה, דאי לאו הכי, וכי לעולם לא תהא נדה? והלא קודם מכה הוה לה וסת:
Tosafot on Niddah 16a:17:1.english: And one Sage holds that [the laws of] fixed cycles are rabbinic - It appears that [this applies] only where she feels that this blood came from the wound, and even so, if it is the time of her fixed cycle, [then] if [the laws of] fixed cycles are Torah law, we are concerned that perhaps the blood also came from the source. But if she does not feel the blood emerging from the wound, she is impure according to everyone if it is the time of her cycle, for if it were not so, would she never become a menstruant? Surely she had a fixed cycle before the wound [occurred]:

Tosafot on Niddah 16a:18:1.hebrew: במקור מקומו טמא קמיפלגי - ורשב"ג לטעמיה בריש תינוקת (לקמן נדה דף סו.). ואע"ג דטומאת בית הסתרים היא, ובפרק דם הנדה (לקמן נדה נה:) אמר נמי דדם בעי רביעית, והכא קאמר טמא אע"ג דליכא רביעית — כדאמרינן בפ' יוצא דופן (לקמן נדה דף מא:): מקור שהזיע כב' טיפי מרגליות טמאה. שמא הכא הלמ"מ הוא; תדע, שהמקור טמא והאשה טהורה:
Tosafot on Niddah 16a:18:1.english: They disagree about whether the place of the source is impure - And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel follows his reasoning in the beginning of [the chapter] Tinokes (below, Niddah 66a). And although it is [a matter of] the impurity of the inner chambers, and in the chapter Dam HaNiddah (below, Niddah 55b) it also says that blood requires a revi'it, and here it says [the blood is] impure even though there is no revi'it — as we say in the chapter Yotzei Dofen (below, Niddah 41b): A source that perspired like two drops of pearls is impure. Perhaps here it is a halakhah transmitted to Moses at Sinai; know [this], for the source is impure while the woman is pure:

Tosafot on Niddah 16a:21:1.hebrew: ב"ש אומרים צריכה ב' עדים על כל תשמיש - פרש"י: ב' עדים חדשים, א' לפני תשמיש ואחד לאחר תשמיש, ומצנעת עד הבקר. ובה"א דיה בב' עדים כל הלילה: אחד לפני תשמיש ראשון ואחד לאחר תשמיש אחרון. [ועוד דמשמע או משמש לאור הנר, אם רוצה להקל כב"ה, ואפילו תשמש לאור הנר צריכה לב"ש בדיקה בכל תשמיש. אבל לפירוש רש"י ולפירוש ר"י א"ש תשמש לאור הנר, פי' שבודקת מיד, מסתמא אם היתה שם טיפת חרדל היתה רואה אפי' על עד ישן. ולפירוש ר"י קיימא שפיר ב"ש אדם שעל העד, אבל לעולם קיימא אדם שבתוך הפה דלישנא בתוך הפה דלישנא בתוך הפה, הכי משמע גי'] וקשה, דלפני תשמיש לא בעו חדשים אלא צנועות. ועוד קשה מה שפירש לב"ה דלא מצרכי לבדוק בכל תשמיש, דלעיל אמר דאינן צנועות עד שבודקות בו לפני תשמיש זה, בודקות בו לפני תשמיש אחר, משמע דבכל תשמיש בודקות. מיהו הא י"ל: בודקות בתשמיש אחר שבלילה שניה. ועוד קשה: מה יודעת מתי שימש באחרונה שתבדוק אחריו? ואם היתה בודקת בשחר כשהיא עומדת, א"כ אינה בודקת סמוך לתשמיש לידע אם בועל בנדות לטמא בועלה ז'. ועוד קשה, דקאמר ב"ש שמא תחפנה שכבת זרע בביאה שניה, היה לו לומר בביאה אחרונה, כיון דלב"ה אינה בודקת עד לאחר תשמיש אחרון. ועוד דב"ה נקט נימוק, וב"ש נקט לישנא אחרינא שמא תחפנה; היה לו לב"ש נמי למינקט נימוק, כיון דקאי על דם שברחם ולא על הדם שעל העד, דהא בית הלל לא מצרכי בדיקה אחר תשמיש ראשון. ועוד דקאמר מדברי כולן נלמד, בעל נפש לא יבעול וישנה, פירוש בלא בדיקה בינתים, אפילו לבעלה גרידא; הא לב"ה אף לטהרות לא צריכה בדיקה. ונראה לר"י כפירוש רשב"ם, דלב"ש צריכה ב' עדים חדשים אחר תשמיש, אחד לו ואחד לה. והא דקתני צריכה, היינו כלומר שהיא מכינה, כדתנן: בנות ישראל משמשות בב' עדים, אחד לו ואחד לה. אע"ג דלפני תשמיש אינה צריכה חדש אלא צנועות, היינו לפי שאין העד מלוכלך כ"כ, אבל לאחר תשמיש שמלוכלך בשכבת זרע צריכות בכל פעם חדש. וב"ה אומרים דיה בב' עדים כל הלילה: מודים שצריכה בדיקה אחר כל תשמיש, אך דלא מצרכי חדש, וטעמא משום דאחר תשמיש איכא רוב לכלוך משכבת זרע ואין ריוח בעד חדש. ואפשר דאפילו צנועות לא בעו חדש לאחר תשמיש, והשתא אתי שפיר הכל:
Tosafot on Niddah 16a:21:1.english: Beit Shammai say she requires two cloths for each act of intercourse - Rashi explained: two new cloths, one before intercourse and one after intercourse, and she stores them away until morning. And according to Beit Hillel, "it is sufficient for her with two cloths for the entire night": one before the first intercourse and one after the last intercourse. [And further, it implies "or she may have intercourse by the light of a lamp" — if she wishes to be lenient like Beit Hillel; and even if she had intercourse by lamplight, according to Beit Shammai she requires an examination after each act of intercourse. But according to Rashi's explanation and Rabbeinu Yitzchak's explanation, "she may have intercourse by lamplight" is fine, meaning that she examines immediately; presumably, if there were a drop [of blood] the size of a mustard seed, she would see it even on an old cloth. And according to Rabbeinu Yitzchak's explanation, Beit Shammai [the term "adam"] stands well as [referring to blood] on the cloth, but in truth it stands as [referring to blood] inside the mouth [of the womb], in the language of "inside the mouth, in the language of, inside the mouth"; this is how the version implies.] But this is difficult: for before intercourse, [the Sages] did not require new cloths, but only that the women be modest. Further, it is difficult what [Rashi] explained according to Beit Hillel, that they do not require her to examine for each act of intercourse; for above it said that they are not modest unless they examine with it before this intercourse [and] examine with it before another intercourse — implying that they examine for every act of intercourse. However, one can say: they examine before another intercourse on the second night. Further, it is difficult: how does she know when he last had intercourse, so that she can examine after it? And if she examined at dawn when she gets up, then she is not examining close to the intercourse, to know whether he had intercourse with a niddah, thereby rendering the one who had relations with her impure for seven days. Further, it is difficult that Beit Shammai said, "lest the semen erode it" in the second act of intercourse; it should have said "in the last act of intercourse," since according to Beit Hillel she does not examine until after the last intercourse. Further, Beit Hillel stated a reason, whereas Beit Shammai stated different wording, "lest it erode it"; Beit Shammai too should have stated a reason, since it relates to blood in the womb and not to blood on the cloth, for Beit Hillel do not require examination after the first intercourse. Further, it said, "From the words of all of them we learn that a person of conscience should not have intercourse and repeat," meaning without an examination in between, even for her husband alone; yet according to Beit Hillel she does not require an examination even for [handling] pure foods. And it appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak [that one should explain] like the explanation of the Rashbam: that according to Beit Shammai she requires two new cloths after intercourse, one for him and one for her. And that which it taught "she requires," it means that she prepares, as we learned: "Jewish women have intercourse with two cloths, one for him and one for her." Although before intercourse she does not require a new one but only [that the women be] modest, that is because the cloth is not so soiled; but after intercourse, when it is soiled with semen, they require a new one each time. And Beit Hillel say "it is sufficient for her with two cloths for the entire night": they agree that she requires an examination after each act of intercourse, but that they do not require a new cloth; and the reason is that after intercourse there is mostly soiling from the semen and there is no benefit in a new cloth. And it is possible that even the modest women did not require a new one after intercourse. And now everything works out well:

Tosafot on Niddah 16a:6:1.hebrew: וחוששת לראייתה - פרש"י: לענין מעת לעת. אע"ג דקי"ל כרבי דוסא דאשה שיש לה וסת דיה שעתה, שלא בשעת וסת מודה דמטמא למפרע. ועוד י"ל דהכא מיירי לענין שתהא מקולקלת למניינה:
Tosafot on Niddah 16a:6:1.english: And she must be concerned for her seeing - Rashi explained: with regard to [the period of] a full day-and-night (onah to onah). Even though we rule like Rabbi Dosa, that a woman who has a fixed cycle [need only be concerned for the impurity from] her [present] hour — [that is, her "hour suffices"] — [nevertheless,] when it is not at the time of her cycle, he agrees that she renders [items] impure retroactively. And furthermore, it can be said that here [the Gemara] is speaking with regard to her [cycle] becoming disrupted in its count.

Tosafot on Niddah 16a:6:2.hebrew: אלמא וסתות דאורייתא - השתא סבר: הא דנקט "ראתה", לאשמועינן דחוששת לראייתה, ולא חשבינן לה כאילו ודאי ראתה מזמן הוסת. וה"ה דכי לא ראתה חוששת. ואם תאמר, היאך רוצה להוכיח דוסתות דאורייתא? והלא אפי' אי וסתות דרבנן, כיון דראתה עכשיו, טמאה גם מזמן הוסת מספק. וי"ל: הני מילי לטהרות, אבל מקולקלת למניינה לא הויא:
Tosafot on Niddah 16a:6:2.english: Evidently, fixed periods are by Torah law - Now [Rav Nachman] holds that the reason [Rav] stated "she saw" is to teach that she must be concerned for her seeing [only], and we do not consider her as though she certainly saw from the time of the period. And the same applies [by extension] even when she did not see, that she is concerned. And if you ask: How does he wish to prove that fixed periods are by Torah law? But even if fixed periods are [only] rabbinic, since she has now seen [blood], she is impure also from the time of the period, out of uncertainty! And one can answer: This applies only to [the status of] pure items, but [the rule that] she is deemed to have disrupted her count is not the case.

Tosafot on Niddah 16a:7:1.hebrew: אלמא וסתות דרבנן - וא"ת דלעיל (נדה דף טו.) אמר רב הונא: לא שנו אלא שלא הגיע שעת וסתה כו', אלמא וסתות דאורייתא? וי"ל דהכא קאמר משמיה דרב, וליה לא ס"ל. ואליבא דרב איכא לקמן ב' לשונות; אי נמי לעיל אתי כלישנא קמא דהכא:
Tosafot on Niddah 16a:7:1.english: Evidently, [the laws of] periods are rabbinic - And if you ask: Above (Niddah 15a), Rav Huna said, "They taught [this] only where the time of her period had not arrived, etc." — evidently, [the laws of] periods are Torah law? And one can answer that here he says [this] in the name of Rav, and he himself does not hold [so]. And according to Rav there are two versions below; alternatively, the statement above accords with the first version here:
